biography: Carlos Campos, a name synonymous with raw aggression and relentless ambition in the Brazilian racing scene, hails from the vibrant favelas of São Paulo. Growing up amidst the cacophony of roaring engines and the intoxicating scent of gasoline from the nearby Interlagos circuit, Carlos’s destiny was practically preordained. His foray into motorsport began humbly, scavenging discarded parts to assemble makeshift go-karts, tearing through the narrow, winding streets of his neighborhood. A chance encounter with a local racing patron during an impromptu street race led to a scholarship at a regional racing academy, where his natural talent quickly blossomed. Campos carved a reputation as a fearless, bordering on reckless, driver, earning podium finishes and the admiration of his countrymen. After a decade of dominating the South American racing scene, he joined the privateer Sport team, but his performance began to decline, and the once-promising star is now facing an uncertain future.
drivingStyle: Campos embodies a high-risk, high-reward driving style. He thrives on late braking maneuvers and audacious overtaking attempts, often pushing his car – and his competitors – to the absolute limit. Tire management isn't his forte; he favors outright pace over strategic conservation, frequently sacrificing late-race performance for early dominance. Under pressure, Campos tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to costly mistakes. His approach is simple: attack every corner as if it's the last, a philosophy that has both won him races and lost him championships.
rivalries: Ricardo Esteves - Campos and Esteves have a long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision that cost Esteves the championship in 2018.
Isabella Rossi - Rossi and Campos share a mutual disdain, with Rossi publicly criticizing Campos's reckless driving and Campos dismissing Rossi as 'too cautious'.
Marco Oliveira - Oliveira and Campos have clashed multiple times on track, with their intense battles often resulting in damaged cars and heated exchanges in the paddock.
quirks: Always wears the same faded Senna t-shirt under his racing suit.
Refuses to start a race without listening to a specific samba song.
Has a habit of adjusting his gloves exactly seven times before getting into the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about finesse; it's about heart. If you ain't willing to risk it all, you ain't a racer."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Stock Car Championship in 2017, after a season-long battle against factory-backed teams, proving that passion and skill could overcome financial limitations.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Interlagos Grand Prix in 2020, a devastating blow that shattered his hopes of securing a coveted spot in a top-tier racing series.
